headline: Oil prices spike as Trump rejects Iran truce offer
summary: Brent crude jumps back above $106 a barrel after the US president declined a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
details: Oil prices surged on Monday as President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal for a seven-day truce to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran had proposed a halt in hostilities at the UN General Assembly to ease a global supply crisis caused by the closure of the vital waterway.
Trump told reporters outside the White House, "I reject their proposal," stating that Iran had "overplayed their hand" and the offer was not the deal he wanted.
Brent crude prices bounced back to over $106 a barrel, reversing a brief dip following the initial news of the truce offer.
The price spike has renewed inflation concerns and negatively impacted stock markets in Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai, Manila, Bangkok, and Jakarta.
Iran continues to demand the release of frozen assets, the lifting of oil sanctions, and an end to the US naval blockade as conditions for reopening the Strait.
Despite the rejection, reports suggest that indirect talks between Washington and Tehran could resume as early as Monday.
The market remains cautious as investors await key US inflation and jobs reports ahead of the Federal Reserve's October policy meeting.
caption:
Oil prices jump back above $106 a barrel after Donald Trump rejects Iran's truce offer.

Oil prices surged on Monday as President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal for a seven-day truce to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Tehran had proposed a halt in hostilities at the UN General Assembly to ease a global supply crisis caused by the closure of the vital waterway.

Trump told reporters outside the White House, "I reject their proposal," stating that Iran had "overplayed their hand" and the offer was not the deal he wanted.

Brent crude prices bounced back to over $106 a barrel, reversing a brief dip following the initial news of the truce offer.

The price spike has renewed inflation concerns and negatively impacted stock markets in Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai, Manila, Bangkok, and Jakarta.

Iran continues to demand the release of frozen assets, the lifting of oil sanctions, and an end to the US naval blockade as conditions for reopening the Strait.

Despite the rejection, reports suggest that indirect talks between Washington and Tehran could resume as early as Monday.

The market remains cautious as investors await key US inflation and jobs reports ahead of the Federal Reserve's October policy meeting.

headline: 5 killed in separate road accidents in Lalmonirhat and Gazipur
summary: Three died in a truck-auto-rickshaw collision in Patgram, while a mother and her young daughter were killed by an unidentified vehicle in Pubail.
details: Five people died in separate road accidents in Lalmonirhat and Gazipur today. In Patgram, a head-on collision between a goods-laden truck and a CNG-run auto-rickshaw killed three people and left seven others injured.

According to Patgram Police Station OC Saiful Islam, the truck driver lost control and rammed into the auto-rickshaw before crashing into a roadside shop. Two victims died on the spot, and one died later at the Patgram Upazila Health Complex.
Five of the injured are in critical condition and have been referred to Rangpur Medical College Hospital. Police have seized the truck, but the driver and helper fled the scene.
In a separate tragedy in Pubail, Gazipur, a woman and her three-and-a-half-year-old daughter were killed after being hit by an unidentified vehicle early this morning.
The victims were identified as 30-year-old Rujuka Begum and her daughter Yamni. They were declared dead after being taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital.
Pubail Police Sub-Inspector Md Anwar Islam stated that the vehicle fled the scene immediately after the accident. Police are currently investigating the circumstances of the crash.
